title: Extending Ultrametric Integral Cryptanalysis
summary: The theory is developed for p equals q equals 2, while its extension to arbitrary primes and all commutative inverse monoids remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Ultrametric integral cryptanalysis is developed in the case $p=q=2$, while extending the theory to arbitrary primes $p$ and to all commutative inverse monoids remains an open task. The target is a general formulation and corresponding extension of the cryptanalysis results over these broader algebraic settings, including $F_n^q$ equipped with multiplication; for $p\ge 5$, the theory must be defined over the $p$-adic numbers $\mathbb{Q}_p$. This extension is expected to generalize the existing results, but its development requires additional technical background.

scope.domain: This concerns ultrametric integral cryptanalysis over broader algebraic settings, including commutative inverse monoids.
parameters: p: prime parameter, fixed at 2 in the current development and generalized to arbitrary primes in the open extension
q: parameter, fixed at 2 in the current development and appearing in F_n^q
F_n^q: multiplication-equipped setting included in the target extension
Q_p: p-adic number system required when p is at least 5
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a general formulation and extend the cryptanalysis results to arbitrary primes and all commutative inverse monoids, including F_n^q with multiplication; for p at least 5, define the theory over the p-adic numbers Q_p.

progress.summary: The source presents the extension as future work, targeting all primes and all commutative inverse monoids, including F_n^q with multiplication. It notes that p-adic numbers Q_p are required when p is at least 5, that more technical background is needed, and that the existing results generalize to the broader setting.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Ultrametric integral cryptanalysis
